brief:
TB-01 Training Building: the project brief

This is the building you model through the whole course. It is fictional. Every number below comes from checker/bimcheck/spec.py, the same file the checker reads, so the brief and the checks always agree. Lengths are in metres; levels are measured from Level 0 (+0.000).

Drawings: Level 1 framing plan, section through grid 2, foundation plan.

Project and site

Item Value
Project name TB-01 Training Building
Site name TB-01 Site
Building name TB-01
Latitude, longitude 38.7369, -9.1427 (a fictional plot in Lisbon)
Elevation of Level 0 above sea level 90.0 m
True north 12 degrees clockwise from project north (+Y)
Units metres (or millimetres)

Levels

Level Elevation
Foundation -1.200
Level 0 +0.000
Level 1 +3.600
Level 2 +7.200
Roof +10.800

Structural levels are at the top of the structural slab. The Foundation level is the underside of the pad footings.

Grid

Axis Position Direction
A x = 0.000 parallel to Y
B x = 6.000 parallel to Y
C x = 12.000 parallel to Y
D x = 18.000 parallel to Y
1 y = 0.000 parallel to X
2 y = 7.000 parallel to X
3 y = 14.000 parallel to X

Grid lines extend 2 m past the outer grids.

Ground floor structure (Level 0 to Level 1)

  • Columns: 400 x 400 mm at all 12 grid intersections, named by grid (C-A1 ... C-D3), from +0.000 up to the slab soffit +3.350. Concrete C30/37, exposure XC1.
  • Core walls: four load-bearing walls, 250 mm thick, forming a core from x 7.5 to 10.5 and y 9.0 to 12.0 (outside faces), from +0.000 to +3.350. The architect's model (datasets/architect_model.ifc) holds the same walls; trace them from it.
  • Level 1 slab: 250 mm, top +3.600, edges at the outer column faces (x -0.2 to 18.2, y -0.2 to 14.2). Two openings: the core (x 7.75 to 10.25, y 9.25 to 11.75) and the stair (x 13.0 to 14.2, y 1.0 to 6.4). Volume 63.06 m3.
  • Beams: on every grid line, between column faces, 300 wide x 350 deep below the soffit (+3.000 to +3.350). Model only the downstand: the slab above is not counted twice. Names: B-1/AB means the beam on grid 1 between grids A and B. 17 beams.
  • Stair: one straight flight, 1.2 m wide between x 13.0 and 14.2, starting at y 1.0 and rising in +Y: 20 risers of 180 mm, treads 280 mm, The last riser is at y 6.32; the slab opening ends at y 6.40, and the 80 mm between them is the top step onto the slab (a short top tread in Bonsai; in FreeCAD the slab edge closes it). Concrete C30/37.

Foundations

  • Pad footings: 1.8 x 1.8 x 0.6 m under every column, top -0.600, named F-A1 ... F-D3. Concrete C25/30, exposure XC2.
  • Pile cap PC-1: 4.0 x 4.0 x 1.0 m centred on the core (x 9.0, y 10.5), top -0.600.
  • Piles: four, 600 mm diameter, 12 m long, 1.2 m each way from the core centre, from the underside of the cap. Concrete C25/30.

Not modelled in this course: the column stubs and core walls between the foundations (-0.600) and Level 0, the ground slab, and starter bars and laps. That is why columns and walls start at +0.000.

Reinforcement (exercise 3.4)

  • Steel grade A500 (A500 NR, the Portuguese designation of a 500 MPa ribbed bar; B500B or B500C in EN 1992-1-1 and EN 10080 terms).
  • Column C-A1: 8 vertical bars Ø16 (four corners and four mid-sides), links Ø8 at 150 mm, 30 mm nominal cover to the links.
  • Footing F-A1: bottom mesh Ø16 at 150 mm each way, centred in the footing (12 bars each way, from -825 to +825 mm about the footing centre), 50 mm cover (the footing is cast on blinding; concrete cast directly against soil needs at least 75 mm).

Data

Element Concrete Exposure Fire resistance Type name
Columns C30/37 XC1 R90 RC Column 400x400
Beams C30/37 XC1 R60 RC Beam 300x350 downstand
Slab C30/37 XC1 REI60
Core walls C30/37 XC1 REI90
Pad footings C25/30 XC2 Pad Footing 1800x1800x600
Pile cap and piles C25/30 XC2
Stair C30/37 XC1

Custom property set TB01_Structural: FireResistance (above) and DesignWorkingLife = 50.

Drawings to produce (sections 5 and 6)

  • Sheet S-101, title LEVEL 1 FRAMING PLAN, scale 1:100.
  • Revisions: A First issue; B Core walls revised.
  • Detail title: TYPICAL COLUMN FOOTING DETAIL.

The concrete classes and exposure classes follow EN 206 and Eurocode 2 notation. They are a reasonable choice for a teaching model, not a design: a real project sets them from its own exposure and the National Annex.

Units: metres (or millimetres).
Site latitude 38.7369, longitude -9.1427, elevation of Level 0 90.0 m above sea level.
True north 12 degrees clockwise from project north (the +Y axis of the model).
1.1.goal: Start the TB-01 model: name the project, the site and the building, use metric units, and place the site on the map with its true north.

steps.bonsai:
Bonsai works in IFC directly: the file you save is tb01.ifc. The panels below are in the Properties editor on the right of the screen. Pick a Bonsai tab with the icons at the top of that editor (Project Overview, Object Information, Geometry and Materials, Drawings and Documents, Costing and Scheduling, Quality and Coordination). The sidebar of the 3D viewport opens with N.

  1. Start Blender with Bonsai enabled. Choose File > New IFC Project > New Metric (m) Project. Bonsai creates an IFC4 project in metres with My Project, My Site, My Building and My Storey.
  2. In the Outliner, click IfcProject/My Project. In Object Information > Object > Object Attributes, click Edit, set Name to TB-01 Training Building and click Save Attributes.
  3. Do the same for IfcSite/My Site (Name TB-01 Site) and IfcBuilding/My Building (Name TB-01).
  4. Select the site again and click Edit in Object Attributes. Type the location as degrees, minutes, seconds and millionths of a second, in square brackets:
    • RefLatitude [38, 44, 12, 840000] (38.7369)
    • RefLongitude [-9, -8, -33, -720000] (-9.1427, every part negative)
    • RefElevation 90
  5. Click Save Attributes.
  6. Open Project Overview > Geometry > Georeferencing and expand its True North subpanel. It says "No True North Found". Click the pencil (Enable Editing True North).
  7. Type -12 in Angle. Bonsai counts angles anticlockwise, so -12 means 12 degrees clockwise. Abscissa becomes 0.2079 and Ordinate 0.9781. Click Edit True North.
  8. Check Project Overview > Geometry > Units: the length unit is the metre.
  9. Choose File > Save IFC Project (Ctrl+S) and save as tb01.ifc in your course folder. File > Save saves only the Blender file, not the IFC.

If this does not work: the site fields only accept whole numbers in the list. Check that you typed four integers, separated by commas, inside square brackets.
steps.freecad:
In FreeCAD you build TB-01 as a normal FreeCAD document (tb01.FCStd) with the BIM workbench, and export it to IFC at the end of every exercise. From section 4 on you open that IFC file and edit it directly.

  1. Start FreeCAD 1.1 and switch to the BIM workbench: View > Workbench > BIM.
  2. Manage > BIM Setup. Set Preferred working units to Millimeters and press OK. FreeCAD always writes IFC files in metres, so millimetres here are only for typing.
  3. Manage > Setup Project. Tick Create a New BIM Project, choose Create a new document without IFC support and type the Project name TB-01 Training Building.
  4. Tick Create Site. Name TB-01 Site, Latitude 38.7369, Longitude -9.1427, Elevation 90 m. Leave Declination at 0; you set it in step 9.
  5. Tick Create Building. Name TB-01. Number of V axes 4, Distance between V axes 6000 mm, Number of H axes 3, Distance between H axes 7000 mm. You finish these axes in exercise 1.3.
  6. In Levels set Number of levels 4 and Level height 3600 mm. You finish the levels in exercise 1.2.
  7. Clear Add Human Figure and press OK. The tree now shows TB-01 Site > TB-01 > Building Layout, Level 0 ... Level 3.
  8. Select TB-01 Site in the tree. In the property editor (Data tab, group Site) check Latitude, Longitude and Elevation (90000 mm).
  9. Still on the site, set Declination to -12 °. FreeCAD counts this angle counter-clockwise, so -12 ° puts true north 12 degrees clockwise from project north.
  10. Name the IFC project. FreeCAD 1.1 has no button for the classic project object, so open View > Panels > Python Console and run:
    import Arch
Arch.makeProject([FreeCAD.ActiveDocument.getObjectsByLabel("TB-01 Site")[0]], name="TB-01 Training Building")
    A TB-01 Training Building object appears at the top of the tree, with the site inside it.
  11. File > Save As…, tb01.FCStd.
  12. Select TB-01 Training Building in the tree. File > Export…, set the file type to Industry Foundation Classes (*.ifc) and save as tb01.ifc. Export this way, with the project selected, at the end of every exercise up to 3.6.

If this does not work: if the checker reports the project name as Unnamed, step 10 was skipped; without the project object FreeCAD names the IfcProject after the internal document name.

1.1.title: Project, site, building, units and location
1.1.why: Every other model on the project (architecture, MEP, survey) must land in the same place. Names, units and location are the first thing a coordinator checks when two models do not line up. Project north is the drawing's 'up'; true north is the real one, and the angle between them drives orientation, sun studies and the setting out on site.

build: Foundation -1.200, Level 0 +0.000, Level 1 +3.600, Level 2 +7.200, Roof +10.800.
Use exactly these names; they are how the checker (and your colleagues) find the levels.
All levels belong to the building TB-01.
1.2.goal: Create the five levels of TB-01 at their structural elevations.

steps.bonsai:
1. Open tb01.ifc with File > Open IFC Project if it is not open.
  2. Go to Project Overview > Spatial > Spatial Decomposition. The list shows the project, site, building and My Storey. The right column of each storey is its elevation.
  3. Double-click My Storey in the list and rename it Level 0. Leave its elevation at 0.
  4. Click the row TB-01 (the building). In the dropdown above the list choose IfcBuildingStorey and click the + button (Add Part to Object). A new storey appears under the building.
  5. Double-click the new storey's name and type Foundation. Double-click its elevation and type -1.2. Bonsai moves the storey to that height.
  6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 for Level 1 at 3.6, Level 2 at 7.2 and Roof at 10.8.
  7. Check that the five storeys are listed under TB-01 and nothing else is.
  8. Click the Level 0 row and click Set Default. New elements go into the default storey, and the panel header shows "Default: Level 0".
  9. Save with File > Save IFC Project.

If this does not work: if a storey ends up under the site or the project, delete it with the X button (Delete Container), click the building row again and add it once more.
steps.freecad:
1. Open tb01.FCStd. In the tree, expand TB-01 Training Building > TB-01 Site > TB-01. Setup Project made Level 0 to Level 3 at 0, 3600, 7200 and 10800 mm.
  2. Select Level 3, press F2 and rename it Roof.
  3. Click an empty part of the 3D view so that nothing is selected (the Level tool puts the selected objects inside the new level).
  4. 3D/BIM > Level. A new level appears in the tree.
  5. Rename it Foundation. In the property editor (Data tab) open Placement > Position and set z to -1200 mm.
  6. If Foundation is not inside TB-01, drag it onto TB-01 in the tree.
  7. Check each level's Placement > Position > z: Level 0 0, Level 1 3600 mm, Level 2 7200 mm, Roof 10800 mm. FreeCAD writes this height as the storey elevation (the Elevation attribute follows it).
  8. Save, select TB-01 Training Building and export tb01.ifc (File > Export…, Industry Foundation Classes).

1.2.title: Levels (building storeys)
1.2.why: In IFC a level is an IfcBuildingStorey: elements are placed in one, and schedules, drawings and quantities are organised by it. Structural levels are usually at the top of the structural slab, which is a few centimetres below the architect's finished floor level; agree which one you model before you start.

build: Lettered axes A, B, C, D parallel to Y at x = 0, 6, 12, 18 m.
Numbered axes 1, 2, 3 parallel to X at y = 0, 7, 14 m.
Each axis must run across the whole building (A to D lines from below grid 1 to beyond grid 3, and so on). Grid lines extend 2 m past the outer grids (see the brief).
1.3.goal: Draw the structural grid that every element will be set out from.

steps.bonsai:
Bonsai's Add Grids button makes a rectangular grid: lettered U axes run along X and numbered V axes ("01", "02"...) run along Y. The brief wants the opposite, so you set the spacings and then swap the labels.

  1. Go to Project Overview > Spatial > Grids and click Add Grids.
  2. Move the mouse over the 3D viewport and choose Edit > Adjust Last Operation (F9). Set U Spacing 7, Number of U Grids 3, V Spacing 6, Number of V Grids 4.
  3. You now have horizontal axes A, B, C at y = 0, 7, 14 and vertical axes 01 to 04 at x = 0, 6, 12, 18. Every axis runs 2 m past the outer axes.
  4. In the Outliner, double-click IfcGridAxis/A and type 1. Bonsai writes the new name into the axis tag. Rename B to 2 and C to 3.
  5. Now rename the vertical axes: 01 to A, 02 to B, 03 to C, 04 to D. Rename the horizontal ones first, as in step 4, or Blender adds ".001" to a duplicate name.
  6. Check in the 3D viewport that A to D run along Y and 1 to 3 run along X.
  7. Save with File > Save IFC Project.

If this does not work (for example the Adjust Last Operation panel does not appear): delete the grid in the Outliner (select it, X, IFC Delete). Open the Scripting workspace, click New in the Text Editor, paste the script below and click Run Script. Then save with File > Save IFC Project and reload with File > Revert IFC Project so the axes appear in the viewport.

import numpy as np
import ifcopenshell.api
import bonsai.tool as tool

f = tool.Ifc.get()
run = ifcopenshell.api.run
level0 = [s for s in f.by_type("IfcBuildingStorey") if s.Name == "Level 0"][0]
grid = run("root.create_entity", f, ifc_class="IfcGrid", name="Structural Grid")
run("geometry.edit_object_placement", f, product=grid)
run("spatial.assign_container", f, relating_structure=level0, products=[grid])
for tag, x in {"A": 0.0, "B": 6.0, "C": 12.0, "D": 18.0}.items():   # parallel to Y, 2 m past grids 1 and 3
    axis = run("grid.create_grid_axis", f, axis_tag=tag, uvw_axes="UAxes", grid=grid)
    run("grid.create_axis_curve", f, p1=np.array([x, -2.0, 0.0]), p2=np.array([x, 16.0, 0.0]), grid_axis=axis)
for tag, y in {"1": 0.0, "2": 7.0, "3": 14.0}.items():              # parallel to X, 2 m past grids A and D
    axis = run("grid.create_grid_axis", f, axis_tag=tag, uvw_axes="VAxes", grid=grid)
    run("grid.create_axis_curve", f, p1=np.array([-2.0, y, 0.0]), p2=np.array([20.0, y, 0.0]), grid_axis=axis)
print("Grid axes:", [a.AxisTag for a in f.by_type("IfcGridAxis")])
steps.freecad:
Setup Project (exercise 1.1) made two axis objects, Vertical Axes and Horizontal Axes, joined in the axis system Axes inside the group Building Layout. FreeCAD exports an axis system with two sets of axes as one IfcGrid. Here you give them the TB-01 tags, lengths and positions.

  1. Open tb01.FCStd and switch to the top view: View > Standard Views > 2 Top.
  2. Select Vertical Axes. Check in the Data tab that Distances reads 0, 6000, 6000, 6000 (axes at x = 0, 6, 12, 18 m).
  3. In the View tab set Numbering Style to A,B,C. These are the lettered axes A to D, parallel to Y.
  4. In the Data tab set Length to 18000 mm (14 m between grids 1 and 3, plus 2 m at each end) and Placement > Position > y to -2000 mm.
  5. Rename the object Grid A-D (F2).
  6. Select Horizontal Axes. Check that Distances reads 0, 7000, 7000 and that Placement > Angle is 90 °.
  7. In the View tab set Numbering Style to 1,2,3.
  8. In the Data tab set Length to 22000 mm and Placement > Position > x to 20000 mm. Turned 90 °, these axes run from x = +20 m back to x = -2 m, at y = 0, 7 and 14 m.
  9. Rename the object Grid 1-3.
  10. Check the drawing: bubbles A to D at the bottom and top, 1 to 3 at both ends, every line 2 m past the outer grids.
  11. Save and export tb01.ifc as before.

If this does not work: axes made one by one with Annotation > Axis are exported as loose IfcGridAxis items without an IfcGrid. Select both axis objects and use Annotation > Axis System to join them.

1.3.title: Structural grid
1.3.why: The grid is the contract between all disciplines: drawings, site setting out and coordination meetings all refer to 'B/2', not to coordinates. In IFC it is an IfcGrid with IfcGridAxis objects, each with a tag (A, 1...) that other programs can read.

build: 400 x 400 mm columns at all 12 grid intersections.
From Level 0 (+0.000) up to the underside of the Level 1 slab (+3.350), not to +3.600: the slab is modelled on its own and nothing is counted twice.
Name each column by its grid position: C-A1, C-A2, ... C-D3.
Place the columns in Level 0.
2.1.goal: Place the twelve ground floor columns.

steps.bonsai:
Bonsai's element tools place occurrences of a type. You make the column type here; exercise 4.1 then only checks it.

  1. Go to Geometry and Materials > Materials. Click the import icon (Load Materials), then + (Add Material). Name it Concrete C30/37, Category concrete, and click OK. New types take the first material in the file, so create this one before any type.
  2. Go to Geometry and Materials > Profiles and click the import icon (Load Profiles). Choose IfcRectangleProfileDef in the dropdown and click + (Add Profile).
  3. Double-click "New Profile" in the list and rename it RC 400x400. Click the pencil (Enable Editing Profile), set XDim 0.4 and YDim 0.4, and click the check mark (Edit Profile).
  4. In Project Overview > Spatial > Spatial Decomposition, click the Level 0 row and click Set Default.
  5. In the toolbar on the left of the 3D viewport, pick the Column Tool. The tool header says "No IfcColumnTypes Found". Click it to open the Type Manager, then click Create New IfcColumnType.
  6. In the dialog set Name RC Column 400x400, Predefined Type COLUMN, Representation Extruded Profile, Profile RC 400x400, and click OK.
  7. In the tool header set Axis to mid-depth centre and H (height) to 3.35. The column runs from Level 0 up to the slab soffit, not to +3.600.
  8. Click Add (Shift+A), click once anywhere in the viewport, then right-click to stop. Bonsai places one column on Level 0.
  9. With the column selected, open the sidebar (N) > Item and set Location X 0, Y 0, Z 0.
  10. In the Outliner, double-click the column and rename it C-A1.
  11. Copy it along grid 1: press Shift+D, X, type 6, Enter. Repeat twice more for x = 12 and 18.
  12. Select the four columns on grid 1. Press Shift+D, Y, 7, Enter, then repeat once more for y = 14.
  13. Rename every column in the Outliner by its grid: C-A1, C-B1 ... C-D3 (letter for x, number for y).
  14. Check that Object Information > Object > Spatial Container says Level 0 for a column. Save with File > Save IFC Project.

If this does not work: if a column stands on the wrong level, check that Level 0 was the default container before you clicked Add, then set the Location Z to 0.
steps.freecad:
1. Open tb01.FCStd. In the tree, right-click Level 0 and tick Active. New objects now go into Level 0.
  2. Turn on Snapping > Snap Intersection (and leave the other snaps on).
  3. 3D/BIM > Column. In the task panel set Length 400 mm, Width 400 mm and Height 3350 mm (up to the slab soffit, not to +3.600). Tick Continue so the tool stays on.
  4. Click the intersection of grids A and 1. The column is centred on the point you click. If the snap is hard to hit, type the point in the X, Y, Z boxes of the task panel and press Enter (A1 is 0, 0, 0).
  5. Click the other 11 intersections: x = 0, 6000, 12000, 18000 for A to D and y = 0, 7000, 14000 for 1 to 3. Press Esc when done.
  6. Rename every column by its grid position (select, F2): C-A1, C-A2, C-A3, C-B1 ... C-D3. Use Placement > Position in the Data tab to see which one is which.
  7. Select one column and check the Data tab: Ifc Type is Column, Predefined Type (group IFC Attributes) is COLUMN, Height is 3350 mm.
  8. Make sure the 12 columns are inside Level 0 in the tree; drag any that are not.
  9. Right-click Level 0 and clear Active.
  10. Save and export tb01.ifc (select TB-01 Training Building, File > Export…, Industry Foundation Classes).

2.1.title: Columns
2.1.why: Columns at grid intersections are the simplest structural element, but they teach the three habits every model needs: exact setting out from the grid, a clear top and bottom, and a mark that matches the drawings. Stopping the column at the slab soffit keeps the concrete quantities right (exercise 2.5).

build: Open or link datasets/architect_model.ifc as a reference. It holds four load-bearing core walls (A-Core-1 to 4) and two partitions that are not yours to model.
Model four 250 mm walls on the architect's core walls: outside faces x 7.5 to 10.5, y 9.0 to 12.0.
From +0.000 to the slab soffit +3.350, in Level 0.
Mark them load-bearing (Pset_WallCommon.LoadBearing = True).
2.2.goal: Link the architect's model and model the structural core walls exactly where the architect placed their load-bearing walls.

steps.bonsai:
1. Go to Project Overview > Project Setup > Links and click Link IFC. Pick datasets/architect_model.ifc. The architect's walls appear in the viewport as a linked model you cannot edit.

  2. Pick the Explore Tool in the toolbar and right-click a core wall of the link. The Links panel lists its attributes and properties (A-Core-1, LoadBearing True). The partitions are not yours.

  3. Pick the Wall Tool. In the tool header click "No IfcWallTypes Found" and then Create New IfcWallType. Set Name RC Wall 250, Predefined Type SOLIDWALL, Representation Vertical Layers, and click OK.

  4. Bonsai gives the new type one 0.1 m layer. In the Type Manager, click the gear next to RC Wall 250 and choose Select Type.

  5. Go to Geometry and Materials > Object Materials. Click the pencil (Enable Editing Assigned Material), then the pencil on the layer (Enable Editing Material Set Item). Set LayerThickness 0.25 and Material Concrete C30/37, click Save Changes, then the check mark (Edit Assigned Material).

  6. Make Level 0 the default container (Spatial Decomposition > Set Default). In the Wall Tool header set RL 0 and H 3.35.

  7. Click Add (Shift+A), click a start point and an end point anywhere, and press Enter. This draws one wall.

  8. In the sidebar (N) > Item, set its Location and Rotation Z, then type the Length in the tool settings (sidebar Tool tab or header L) and click its refresh button (Update):

    Wall Location X, Y Rotation Z Length
    W-Core-S 7.5, 9.0 0 3.0
    W-Core-N 10.5, 12.0 180 3.0
    W-Core-E 10.5, 9.25 90 2.5
    W-Core-W 7.5, 11.75 270 2.5

    The layer lies on the left of the wall's direction, so each wall sits inside the core outline x 7.5 to 10.5, y 9.0 to 12.0. Location Z is 0.

  9. Repeat steps 7 and 8 for the four walls and rename them in the Outliner.

  10. Draw each wall on its own, so the long walls run through the corners and the short walls stop at them, as in the brief. Either way works: if you draw the core as one closed outline, Bonsai mitres the corners, and the volume and the checks are the same.

  11. Select the four walls. Go to Object Information > Misc > Bulk Property Editor > Bulk Add / Edit Custom Properties and click Add Property to Edit. Fill in Pset_WallCommon, LoadBearing, tick the value, data type IfcBoolean, and click Apply Changes.

  12. Compare your walls with the link: in Links, set the link to wireframe with its cube icon. The faces should coincide.

  13. Save with File > Save IFC Project.
steps.freecad:
1. Open tb01.FCStd. 3D/BIM > Generic 3D Tools > External Reference. In the property editor set File to datasets/architect_model.ifc. The architect's walls appear, read-only. Leave this object at the top of the tree, outside TB-01 Training Building, so it is not exported with your model.
  2. In the top view, find the four core walls (x 7.5 to 10.5 m, y 9.0 to 12.0 m). The two partitions elsewhere are not yours.
  3. Right-click Level 0 and tick Active. Turn on Snapping > Snap Midpoint and Snap Endpoint.
  4. 3D/BIM > Wall. In the task panel set Width 250 mm, Height 3350 mm and Alignment Center.
  5. Trace the south wall along its centre line: click the midpoint of its west end, then the midpoint of its east end (7500, 9125 and 10500, 9125; you can also type the points in the X, Y, Z boxes and press Enter).
  6. Trace the other three walls the same way, each with its own two clicks: north 7500, 11875 to 10500, 11875; west 7625, 9250 to 7625, 11750; east 10375, 9250 to 10375, 11750. The west and east walls stop at the inner faces of the south and north walls, so no two walls overlap.
  7. Rename the walls W-Core-S, W-Core-N, W-Core-W, W-Core-E. For each, set Predefined Type (Data tab, group IFC Attributes) to SOLIDWALL; the default is MOVABLE.
  8. Select the four walls. Manage > Manage IFC Properties. In Add property set pick Wall Common (Pset_WallCommon). Set LoadBearing to True and leave the other values empty (empty values are not exported). Press OK.
  9. Select the External Reference and press Space to hide it. Clear Active on Level 0.
  10. Save and export tb01.ifc with TB-01 Training Building selected.

If this does not work: if two walls become one object when you draw them, Edit > Preferences > BIM > General Settings has Auto-join walls ticked; clear it and draw again.

2.2.title: Core walls traced from the architect's model
2.2.why: On a real project you never type the architect's coordinates in again: you link their model and trace (or copy and monitor) the elements that are structural. Linking also shows you at once when the architect moves a wall. Partitions stay in the architect's model.

build: Top of slab +3.600, soffit +3.350.
Edges at the outer column faces: x -0.2 to 18.2, y -0.2 to 14.2.
Core opening x 7.75 to 10.25, y 9.25 to 11.75; stair opening x 13.0 to 14.2, y 1.0 to 6.4.
Place the slab in Level 1. Expected volume: 63.06 m3.
2.3.goal: Model the 250 mm Level 1 slab with the core and stair openings.

steps.bonsai:
1. Pick the Slab Tool (it shares a toolbar button with Roof, Stair Flight and Ramp Flight: click and hold). Click "No IfcSlabTypes Found" and Create New IfcSlabType. Set Name RC Slab 250, Predefined Type FLOOR, Representation Horizontal Layers, and click OK.

  4. Click Add (Shift+A). The status bar must say Offset Type: TOP, so the top of the slab is at Level 1 (+3.600) and its soffit at +3.350. Press O to change it if needed.
  5. Type the four corners instead of clicking. For each corner press Tab until the X field is active, type the value, press Tab once for Y, type the value and press Enter:
    • X -0.2, Y -0.2
    • X 18.2, Y -0.2
    • X 18.2, Y 14.2
    • X -0.2, Y 14.2
  6. Press Enter again to finish. Rename the slab S-L1 in the Outliner.

  8. Make the stair opening the same way: Location 13.6, 3.7, 3.475, Dimensions 1.2, 5.4, 0.45.

  10. Check Object Information > Object > Spatial Container: the slab is in Level 1.
  11. Select the slab and go to Costing and Scheduling > Quantity Take-off > Simple Quantity Calculator. Click Calculate Object Volumes: the result is 63.06 m3.

If this does not work: if the slab sits on top of Level 1 (+3.600 to +3.850), the offset was not TOP. Undo, check the status bar and draw it again.
steps.freecad:
1. Open tb01.FCStd. Right-click Level 1 and tick Active. The working plane moves to Level 1 (+3.600), so what you draw now lies at the top of the slab.
  2. 2D Drafting > Rectangle. Type the first corner -200, -200 in the X and Y boxes and press Enter, then the opposite corner 18200, 14200 and Enter. (If Relative is ticked in the task panel, type the size 18400, 14400 instead.)

2.3.title: Level 1 slab with openings
2.3.why: Openings must be real openings (voids) in the slab, not holes drawn on top of it, or the quantities and every downstream check will be wrong. The checker compares the slab's volume with the brief.

build: One beam on every grid line between two columns: 9 along X (grids 1, 2, 3) and 8 along Y (grids A to D).
300 mm wide, 350 mm deep below the slab soffit (+3.000 to +3.350).
Each beam stops at the column faces (clear spans: 5.6 m along X, 6.6 m along Y).
Name them by grid line and bay: B-1/AB is the beam on grid 1 between A and B. Place them in Level 1.
2.4.goal: Model the 17 downstand beams of Level 1.

steps.bonsai:
1. In Geometry and Materials > Profiles, add an IfcRectangleProfileDef named RC 300x350 with XDim 0.30 (width) and YDim 0.35 (depth).
  2. Pick the Beam Tool (click and hold the Column Tool button). Click "No IfcBeamTypes Found" and Create New IfcBeamType: Name RC Beam 300x350 downstand, Predefined Type BEAM, Representation Extruded Profile, Profile RC 300x350.

steps.freecad:
FreeCAD places a beam on the line between the two points you give, with its section centred on that line. For a 350 mm downstand under the soffit (+3.000 to +3.350) the line is at mid-depth, z = 3175 mm.

  1. Open tb01.FCStd. Right-click Level 1 and tick Active (new beams go into Level 1).
  2. 3D/BIM > Beam. In the task panel set Width 300 mm and Height 350 mm. Tick Global so the points you type are model coordinates, and tick Continue.
  3. Beam B-1/AB on grid 1 between the faces of C-A1 and C-B1: type X 200, Y 0, Z 3175, Enter; then X 5800, Y 0, Z 3175, Enter.

  5. Beams along Y: from y+200 to the next grid y-200, at x = 0, 6000, 12000, 18000, for example B-A/12 from 0, 200, 3175 to 0, 6800, 3175 (8 beams).

If this does not work: if a beam stands on end, you clicked instead of typing the second point at the same Z; delete it and type both points.

2.4.title: Level 1 beams
2.4.why: The full beam is 600 mm deep (350 downstand + 250 slab). Modelling only the downstand is a common convention that keeps the concrete volumes honest. Stopping beams at the column faces does the same at the joints.

build: Fix any overlap between columns, beams, walls and the slab (for example a column running into the slab or a beam running into a column).
Expected volumes: columns 6.43 m3, beams 10.84 m3, walls 9.21 m3, slab 63.06 m3; total 89.54 m3.
2.5.goal: Check that no two elements overlap, and that the concrete volumes of the frame match the brief.

steps.bonsai:
Bonsai has no join command for concrete members. You get clean joints by modelling each element to its true extent, which you did in 2.1 to 2.4. This exercise checks it.

  1. Hide the slab (H) and look at a column head: the beams stop at the column faces and the column stops at +3.350, under the slab.
  2. In Project Overview > Grouping and Filtering > Search, click the funnel icon (Edit Filter Query), type IfcColumn and click OK, then click Search. Bonsai selects the 12 columns.
  3. Go to Costing and Scheduling > Quantity Take-off > Simple Quantity Calculator and click Calculate Object Volumes. The result should be 6.43 m3.
  4. Repeat for IfcBeam (10.84 m3), IfcWall (9.21 m3) and IfcSlab (63.06 m3). Deselect everything (Alt+A) before each search: Search adds to the selection.
  5. If a total is too high, find the element that runs too far. Common causes: a column with height 3.6, a beam with length 6.0, a beam whose Location is on the grid instead of the column face.
  6. Fix a column with its H value and Update, a beam with its Length and Update, or move it in the sidebar (N) > Item.
  7. Unhide everything (Alt+H) and save with File > Save IFC Project.
steps.freecad:
In FreeCAD each element keeps the size you give it, so a clean frame comes from modelling every element to its true extent: columns and walls stop at +3.350, beams stop at the column faces, the slab sits on top.

  1. Open tb01.FCStd. Select all 12 columns and check in the Data tab that Height reads 3350 mm (it shows one value when all agree).
  2. Select the four core walls: Height 3350 mm, Width 250 mm. The west and east walls run from y 9250 to 11750, between the south and north walls.
  3. Select the beams along X: Length 5600 mm; the beams along Y: Length 6600 mm. A beam of 6000 or 7000 mm runs into the columns.
  4. Select the slab: Height 250 mm, base rectangle at z = 3600.
  5. To see an overlap, select two elements and use Modify > Intersection. If the result has a volume, the two elements overlap; fix the size or position, then delete the intersection object.
  6. Look at the volumes in Manage > Manage IFC Quantities: the Volume column shows each element. Expected totals: columns 6.43 m³, beams 10.84 m³, core walls 9.21 m³, slab 63.06 m³.
  7. Close the dialog with Cancel (you add quantities in exercise 7.8). Save and export tb01.ifc.

2.5.title: Clean joints: no element counted twice
2.5.why: Revit handles this with 'join geometry' and structural connections. In open tools you get the same result by modelling each element to its true extent. Overlaps are not just untidy: they double count concrete in quantities and make clash reports noisy.

build: Width 1.2 m between x 13.0 and 14.2; first riser at y 1.0; climbs in +Y.
20 risers of 180 mm (total rise 3.600), treads of 280 mm, arriving at Level 1 inside the opening (y up to 6.4).
Place it in Level 0. If your program can store the number of risers and the riser height, do it.
3.1.goal: Model a straight concrete stair through the stair opening.

steps.bonsai:
Bonsai's parametric stair counts treads, not risers: 19 treads give 20 risers of 3.6 / 20 = 0.180 m. It also draws a full tread at the top, so you shorten the last one to land at y 6.4.

  1. Make Level 0 the default container.
  2. From the Add menu in the 3D viewport header, choose IFC Element. In the dialog set Name ST-1, Definition IfcElement, Class IfcStairFlight, Predefined Type STRAIGHT, Representation Stair, and click OK.
  3. Go to Geometry and Materials > Parametric Geometry > Stair and click the pencil (Enable Editing Stair).
  4. Set Stair Type Concrete, Width 1.2, Height 3.6, Number of Treads 19, Tread Run 0.28, Tread Depth 0.25, Base Slab Depth 0.25, Top Slab Depth 0.25.
  5. Untick Has Top Nib. With it on, the waist runs on under the landing to y 6.67, past the slab edge.
  6. Click Unlock First/Last Treads and set Custom First / Last Treads Widths to 0.28 and 0.08. The last riser is then at y 6.32 and the top tread ends at y 6.40.
  7. Click Finish Editing. The panel shows Number of Risers 20, Tread Rise 0.18 and Length 5.40.
  8. Bonsai builds the flight along its local X, with the width along local Y. In the sidebar (N) > Item set Location 14.2, 1.0, 0 and Rotation Z 90. The flight now climbs in +Y between x 13.0 and 14.2.
  9. Look at the stair in Object Information > Object > Property Sets: Bonsai filled Pset_StairFlightCommon with NumberOfRiser 20 and RiserHeight 0.18.
  10. Check from the side that the top tread meets the slab edge at +3.600. Save with File > Save IFC Project.
steps.freecad:
1. Open tb01.FCStd. Right-click Level 0 and tick Active. Click an empty part of the 3D view so nothing is selected.
  2. 3D/BIM > Stairs. A straight flight appears at the origin.
  3. In the Data tab set Length 5320 mm (19 treads of 280), Width 1200 mm, Height 3600 mm and Number Of Steps 20. Check that Riser Height shows 180 mm and Tread Depth 280 mm.
  4. Leave Align at Left and Structure at Massive. Set Placement: Angle 90 °, Axis 0, 0, 1, Position 13000, 1000, 0. The flight now runs in +Y from y 1.0 m, between x 13.0 and 14.2 m.
  5. Rename it ST-1 and check that it is inside Level 0.
  6. Look at the top step: FreeCAD models 19 treads, up to +3.420. The 20th riser is the edge of the slab opening at Level 1, and the flight ends at y 6.32, inside the opening.
  7. Store the riser count: select ST-1, Manage > Manage IFC Properties. In Add property set pick Stair Common. Set NumberOfRiser 20 and NumberOfTreads 19 and leave the other values empty. Press OK.
  8. Do not fill RiserHeight there: FreeCAD 1.1.3 writes length properties in millimetres into a file whose unit is the metre, so 180 would be read as 180 m. The checker takes the riser height from the geometry.
  9. Clear Active on Level 0. Save and export tb01.ifc.

3.1.title: Stair from Level 0 to Level 1
3.1.why: Stairs are where architecture and structure meet: the structural engineer owns the flight and its supports, the architect owns the going and the headroom. A stair modelled with the right riser count is also checked against building rules (riser height, going) by code-checking tools.

Footing type PAD_FOOTING (set on the footing or on its type), named F-A1 ... F-D3, in the Foundation level.

3.2.title: Pad footings

Four piles (IfcPile), 600 mm diameter, 12 m long, at 1.2 m each way from the core centre, from the underside of the cap (-1.600) down to -13.600.
Everything in the Foundation level.

1. Open tb01.FCStd. Right-click Foundation and tick Active.
  2. Pile cap: 3D/BIM > Column with Length 4000 mm, Width 4000 mm, Height 1000 mm. Tick Global and type the point 9000, 10500, -1600, Enter.

If this does not work: do not make the piles from a Draft circle. In FreeCAD 1.1.3 the IFC export of a circle-based structure with Ifc Type Pile stops with "Cannot create polygon because less than two vertices are given".
